title: System proper/open and projection/exchange pastings respect shifts
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$, uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ work on the small pro-etale sites with $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$ and the strict semilinear system category $\mathscr S_W$ (module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_W$ with compatible semilinear transition maps). Use its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$, total limit $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$, and actual adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ with unit $u$ and counit $e$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. System operations are inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type maps $v$, direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, quasi-compact open extension $J_j$, and derived tensor, with the integral counterparts of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Restrict input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs are derived complete and constructible. Use the fixed slotwise cochain shifts of [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data], with the signed second tensor slot, and the K-injective strict-tower Roos model for total limit. Write $\chi_H:H(M[r])\to H(M)[r]$ for a designated slot, holding other slots fixed. Suppose the primitive, adjunction, direct-image compositor and normalized open $\beta,\gamma$ maps commute with the fixed shifts in each designated slot. For a commutative proper/open square $Q$ with top $k:U\hookrightarrow V$, bottom $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ quasi-compact open, vertical maps $r:U\to W$ and $p:V\to Z$ proper, and $pk=ir$, put $V_W=V\times_ZW$, with projections $b:V_W\to V$, $q:V_W\to W$, and clopen $s=(k,r):U\to V_W$. Use the actual maps of [lem-sf-semilinear-proper-open-mate-pasting]:
$$\lambda_Q:P_iS_pJ_k\cong S_qP_bJ_k\cong S_qJ_s\cong S_qS_s\cong S_r,$$
$$\alpha_Q=(J_bJ_sP_sP_q\cong J_kP_r)\circ J_b\pi_sP_q\circ\beta_{i,p},$$
$$\Gamma_Q=S_pJ_k\varepsilon_r\circ S_p\alpha_QS_r\circ\eta_pJ_iS_r,$$
where $\pi_s:1\to J_sP_s$ is the component projection. Both $\lambda_Q$ and $\Gamma_Q$ commute with all integer shifts, including the noncartesian refinement squares allowed in that statement.
For a cartesian square $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, let $\theta:P_{f'}P_g\cong P_{g'}P_f$ be the canonical pullback comparison. On the admissible system domains where they are defined, the canonical maps
$$\operatorname{Ex}_*=S_{f'}P_{g'}\varepsilon_f\circ S_{f'}\theta S_f\circ\eta_{f'}P_gS_f,\qquad \pi_{p;M,N}=S_p((\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1)\mu_p)\circ\eta_{p,S_pM\otimes N},$$
and for a compactification $f=pj$ and its base change, the maps
$$\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=S_{p'}\beta\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}J_j,\qquad \operatorname{PF}^c=S_p\gamma\circ\pi_{p;J_jM,N}$$
commute naturally with the shift in every input occurrence; $\gamma$ here includes $P_jP_p\cong P_f$. These are the system composites specified by [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] and [def-exchange-projection]. The compactification composition and refinement comparisons obtained by finite pasting of $\Gamma_Q$ and the direct-image/open compositors also commute with these shifts. All equations hold intrinsically in the semilinear-system derived category.

proof.text:
Fix an integer $r$ and one labelled input occurrence, fixing the others. Use the recursive composite shifts of [def-pur-integral-operation-shift-data]. The composition and whiskering rules of [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] apply with the chosen shift $[r]$ in place of $[1]$. In particular, if $\tau:F\to G$ and $\sigma:G\to H$ satisfy their shift squares, then
$$\chi_H(\sigma\tau)_{M[r]}=\sigma_M[r]\chi_G\tau_{M[r]}=(\sigma\tau)_M[r]\chi_F.$$
Whiskering uses the composite comparison $\chi_{HF}=\chi_H\,H(\chi_F)$ and naturality of $\chi_H$. For an invertible $\tau$, its equation gives $\chi_F\tau_{M[r]}^{-1}=(\tau_M[r])^{-1}\chi_G$ by multiplying by the two inverses. Thus finite composites, whiskerings and inverses preserve the required equation. These operations take place in the derived category of whole systems.

proof.text: The word primitive in the hypothesis includes the pullback compositors, square comparisons, tensor comparisons, open compositors, clopen comparison and component projection listed in [lem-pur-system-primitive-comparison-shift]. Use their assumed shift squares with the fixed comparisons of this item. For $\alpha_Q$, its three factors are respectively the assumed normalized $\beta_{i,p}$, $J_b\pi_sP_q$, and the open and pullback compositors. Each satisfies the shift square, so step 1 gives it for $\alpha_Q$. In the displayed formula for $\Gamma_Q$, the outer factors are whiskered unit and counit maps, and the middle factor is $S_p\alpha_QS_r$. The assumed adjunction squares and step 1 therefore give the square for this exact $\Gamma_Q$. The clopen projection is not inverted. The proper/open statement supplies these precise maps also when the square is noncartesian.

source.place: Agent-formulated shift version of the maps-used and adjunction-mates sentences; adic transport Step 2

proof.text: The proper/open statement supplies the isomorphism $\lambda_Q$ and the identity $\lambda_Q\circ P_i\Gamma_Q=1$ under the open unit. More explicitly let $u^i:S_r\xrightarrow{\sim}P_iJ_iS_r$ be the open unit, which is shift compatible by hypothesis. Then $(P_i\Gamma_Q)u^i=\lambda_Q^{-1}$, since composition with the specified isomorphism $\lambda_Q$ is the identity. Step 2 and whiskering show that the left side commutes with shifts. Step 1 applied to its inverse proves the required square for the actual $\lambda_Q$, including its stated clopen factorization. This uses an equality intrinsic to semilinear systems, rather than detecting equality after evaluation. The same identity and argument hold for the refinement squares with $r=1$.

source.place: Agent-formulated shift version of the maps-used and adjunction-mates sentences; adic transport Step 2

proof.text: For the cartesian exchange, $\theta$ is the composite of the primitive pullback compositors and the square identification; it has the assumed shift square. Read the system exchange formula exactly as specified by the system realization statement and [def-exchange-projection]: first $\eta_{f'}P_gS_f$, then $S_{f'}\theta S_f$, then $S_{f'}P_{g'}\varepsilon_f$. Every factor is a whiskered primitive or adjunction map. Step 1 gives the shift equation for $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ in its input. This argument only uses the supplied adjunctions on the admissible domains and does not require $\operatorname{Ex}_*$ to be invertible.

source.place: Agent-formulated shift version of the maps-used and adjunction-mates sentences; adic transport Step 2

proof.text: For the proper projection write $a_{M,N}=(\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1)\mu_{p;S_pM,N}$, so $\pi_{p;M,N}=S_p(a_{M,N})\eta_{p;S_pM\otimes N}$. Fix $N$ and shift $M$. The counit equation and naturality of the first-slot tensor comparison give the equation for $\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1$; the primitive $\mu$ equation gives it for $a$, and the unit equation and step 1 give it for $\pi$. Fix $M$ and shift $N$ instead. Naturality in the fixed first factor $\varepsilon_{p,M}$ of the second-slot comparison gives the same square for $\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1$; compose with the second-slot $\mu$ square and the unit square. This proves the second-slot $\pi$ equation. The comparison in this calculation is the specified signed one, $(-1)^{ri}$ in first degree $i$, throughout; it is never replaced by an unsigned reindexing. Both calculations are natural in the fixed as well as the shifted input.

source.place: Agent-formulated shift version of the maps-used and adjunction-mates sentences; adic transport Step 2

proof.text: For a chosen compactification substitute step 4 into $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=S_{p'}\beta\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{*,p}J_j$. The remaining factor is the assumed normalized open $\beta$, so step 1 gives its shift equation. Substitute step 5 into $\operatorname{PF}^c=S_p\gamma\circ\pi_{p;J_jM,N}$. The normalized $\gamma$ and its pullback compositor have their assumed squares in each slot; hence step 1 gives both projection squares. These are precisely the compactification-relative system composites specified by the realization statement and the exchange/projection definition. Finally induct on the number of factors in any specified composition or refinement pasting: the empty pasting is the identity, and adjoining a whiskered $\Gamma_Q$, a direct-image/open compositor, or an inverse comparison uses steps 1-3. Thus every such finite pasting has its required square. All arguments hold for every integer $r$ and on the stipulated admissible domains. Shifting changes finite bounds by $r$ but preserves the existence of common finite intervals; no new domain-preservation assertion for the operations is used.

The primitive node proves the pi_s and compositor squares unconditionally. Gamma_Q is the whiskered eta/alpha/epsilon composite, exactly as in mate-pasting, refinement squares included. Steps 4-5: Ex_* and pi agree with def-exchange-projection and the realization node. In the second slot, epsilon_M has degree 0, so naturality of the signed comparison in the first factor is correct. Step 6: Ex_!^c and PF^c are whiskerings plus the assumed beta and gamma; the pasting induction has a stated base and step.
